help.cedarloom:
Usage: cedarloom <command> [options]
cloom is a short name for cedarloom.

Commands:
  doctor           Check that this computer and project can run CedarLoom.
  runs list        List the runs recorded for this project.
  runs show <run>  Show a run and its steps.
  undo <run>       Undo a run, as a run of its own.
  workflows list   List the shipped and project workflow definitions.
  workflows show <name>
                   Show a workflow definition.
  workflows validate [<name>...]
                   Check workflow definitions with the plugin's generator.

Options:
  --json           Print one JSON document instead of text.
  --help, -h       Show the usage of a command.
  --version, -V    Print the version of CedarLoom.
help.doctor:
Usage: cedarloom doctor [--plugin-root <dir>] [--json]

Checks that this computer can run CedarLoom: the Node.js version, the project,
the cl-workflow plugin from the CedarLoom marketplace: installed for this
project, new enough and enabled, and the workflow definitions in
.cedarloom/workflows: valid, and their generated files in .claude up to date.
For the definitions it runs the plugin's generator in a temporary folder.

Options:
  --plugin-root <dir>  Use this cl-workflow folder instead of the installed
                       plugin, and run its generator. Its origin is not
                       checked.
help.runs:
Usage: cedarloom runs <verb> [options]

Verbs:
  list        List the runs recorded for this project, newest first.
  show <run>  Show a run and its steps.
help.runs-list:
Usage: cedarloom runs list [--json]

Lists the runs recorded for this project, newest first.
help.runs-show:
Usage: cedarloom runs show <run> [--json]

Shows the run <run> and its steps.
help.undo:
Usage: cedarloom undo <run> [--yes] [--json]

Undoes the run <run> as a run of its own. Without --yes it shows the plan and does not apply it.
help.workflows:
Usage: cedarloom workflows <verb> [options]

Verbs:
  list                List the shipped and project workflow definitions.
  show <name>         Show a workflow definition.
  validate [<name>...]
                      Check workflow definitions with the plugin's generator.
help.workflows-list:
Usage: cedarloom workflows list [--plugin-root <dir>] [--json]

Lists the workflow definitions shipped with the cl-workflow plugin, which are
read only, and the project's own in .cedarloom/workflows. Without a usable
plugin it lists the project's alone.

Options:
  --plugin-root <dir>  Use this cl-workflow folder instead of the installed
                       plugin. Its origin is not checked.
help.workflows-show:
Usage: cedarloom workflows show <name> [--shipped] [--plugin-root <dir>] [--json]

Shows the project's workflow definition <name>: each stage and phase by its
JSON Pointer, then the definition.

Options:
  --shipped            Show the definition shipped with the plugin.
  --plugin-root <dir>  Use this cl-workflow folder instead of the installed
                       plugin. Its origin is not checked.
help.workflows-validate:
Usage: cedarloom workflows validate [<name>...] [--shipped] [--plugin-root <dir>] [--json]

Checks the project's workflow definitions <name>, or all of them, with the
plugin's generator, run in a temporary folder, and prints each problem's file,
field and rule. Exits 1 when a definition has a problem.

Options:
  --shipped            Check the definitions shipped with the plugin.
  --plugin-root <dir>  Use this cl-workflow folder instead of the installed
                       plugin, and run its generator. Its origin is not
                       checked.
output.runs-none: No runs are recorded for this project.
output.undo-no-steps: Every file is already as before run
